title: How much should you bet? Kelly's answer

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You win a bet half the time, and it pays one and a half times your stake. How much of your money should you wager each round?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Kelly criterion has an answer. It sets the bet size from the chance of winning and the payoff ratio. Kelly_RM, an AlgoÉTS research repository, lets you watch it work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: First, a coin-flip game. A biased coin, repeated bets, and four strategies side by side. One bets the Kelly fraction, one learns the odds after ten flips, one bets a fixed amount, and one bets big after three tails.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does the Kelly bettor do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In the notebook's example, about one sixth of its wealth. Bet more, and growth shrinks. At twice the Kelly fraction, growth drops to zero.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then it goes to real markets?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A second notebook downloads price histories, optimizes an R S I strategy with backtesting dot py, measures the win probability for each ticker, and turns that into a Kelly fraction.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So you see the formula first on coins, then on trades.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The full write-up has the charts and the worked example.
